Asked "why is there no Heisenberg?": because it is a property of a sum, the cancellation of the w emitters' rays off the axis, and `beam` counts whole rays and never sums; asked what it helps: to be right about light (the fringes and the fan are measured facts; without the sum the model predicts neither), while the atom's stability and its levels come from the board and not from it; "so the wave belongs in the screen? because in the world behind the detector one sees only waves and not rays": exactly, nature is seen through detectors of a width, an interval and a threshold, and what they deliver is a sum of many rays, which behaves as a wave; a detector narrow and sensitive enough to catch one ray sees a click, a particle: wave and particle are the width and the threshold of the detector, not properties of light.

### 03. THE PRINCIPLE: on the GameBoard a ray, in the world a wave

**THE PRINCIPLE, the owner, 2026-09-20:** "So the mathematics works out: on the game board a ray, and in the world a wave is received." Confirmed by the measurements of the day and recorded as the standing statement of the model: on the board a ray with a record, one law, a bijection, no remainder (the echo forward and back bit-exact); at the gate a sum of the rays that arrived (the one reading function); in the world behind the detector a wave (A10: the record narrows with the width of the opening while the count never does; the two openings: the fringes in the record and never in the count). The label along the unit vector at Q = 64 landed the same hour with the physicist's four corrections (series C identical in its readings, Bell unchanged), and series D under it: at S = 32 and r = 12 the probe stays bound for 2 891 intervals through seven turns (period 289 against 343 derived, the mean radius 11.25) without returning to one Link of its start; the field's bursts and the lattice's grain remain the named causes. The reading of the audit of issue #361 (2026-09-20), adopted and flagged: the principle is a statement about a crowd, not about light in general; a wave is the sum of the events that reach one detector set in one interval, so a single quantum per interval interferes with nothing, and at a low rate the model predicts additive counts, which nature's single-particle experiments contradict (HYPOTHESES section 11; A10 at a low rate measures it). The wave is in the crowd, not in the event; the principle is the model's limit there, stated so that a reader does not take it as a claim about every light.

### 06. The orchestrator's answer to why

The orchestrator's answer to "why", recorded, flagged for the owner to strike: on the GameBoard a NatureBeam is one event at one Node with one direction, one phase and whole numbers; it never splits and the interval is a bijection, so nothing at a Node ever holds a sum of two paths, and a single ray cannot interfere with itself. A detector is a set of Nodes with one record, and its `wave` reading is the pointer P = sum over the arrivals of a_k (cos phi_k, sin phi_k); its square is sum a_k^2 + 2 sum a_j a_k cos(phi_j - phi_k). The first term is the count (the `beam` reading); the second is the interference, present only where one record sums more than one ray with a definite phase difference, which is the path difference in Links times the family's phase per Link. The wave is therefore a reading of a crowd of rays by a set, and it exists in the world because every instrument in the world (an eye, a screen, an antenna) is such a set, reading many rays over many intervals; no instrument reads one ray at one Node in one interval, which is the uncertainty. The measurements of the day stand as the evidence: the count never narrows and the `wave` record narrows with the width (A10); the fringes of series C are in the record and not on the GameBoard; the age reading converts the GameBoard's intervals into the world's clock (M/r) without touching the GameBoard.

Bohr's whole number is de Broglie's: momentum x the length of the orbit = j h, a whole number of the phase's turns along the path, not of the clock's ticks in time; the physicist checked the owner's formulation with the clock (T / K = j) and with Kepler it gives r_j ~ j^(2/3), not j^2. The seven proposals tabled for the owner: (1) a body on a set of Nodes with one record (the electron of width 3; an engine feature, not a law), (2) the strong force as a second density column sigma with the attractive sign, kappa = M_A (rho_A rho_B - sigma_A sigma_B - 1) x flow, (3) its range as a family of sigma rays booked as escaped at a declared age L, (4) the weak force as a table entry that re-releases a measured event as another family, (5) Bohr's turn rule: at every Link a body steps its phase turns by its momentum label, one declared world constant `action` (h), a whole turn per step with the remainder read off the clock, (6) Bohr's closure as a reading: a detector's `wave` record of the rays the electron releases over many turns adds coherently only for an orbit whose phase closes, so the lines appear in the record while the board allows every radius, (7) a feedback from the record to the board so that only closed orbits survive on the board (not recommended). The owner: "Bohr should come out by itself behind the detector; what is missing on the board by the laws?" The answer, flagged: one thing, on the body and not on the detector: a measured event's phase turns only by its own clock (content / K per self-creation), by time alone, so the rays it releases carry to the detector how long and not how far; on the orbit there is no wavelength for the detector to read, and what comes out by itself is the closure in time, j^(2/3). What is missing is the tie between a body's momentum and its phase that E = h f already gives a released ray; with it the detector shows Bohr by itself in the existing `wave` reading, nothing is kept at a Node, the interval stays a bijection and the board allows every radius. DECIDED (the owner): "On Bohr, go, and put it as parameters outside the board like the age." Recorded as the placement rule: the turn is a declared parameter of the measured event, the external thing, read by it from its own record (its momentum label and the Links it stepped, derived from its age by the step rule as the owed count is) with no memory at a Node; the rays' flight and collision are untouched; a world without the key reads the same integer by integer. ### 15. DECIDED: the GameBoard is deterministic; the detector's world is not, by the uncertainty in the detector's world

**DECIDED: the GameBoard is deterministic; the detector's world is not, by the uncertainty in the detector's world (the owner, 2026-09-20).** The owner's words, translated: "Record in Highlights if it is not there: the GameBoard is deterministic. The detector's world is not, because of the uncertainty principle in the detector's world. That is correct, no?" Recorded as the standing statement, with the orchestrator's reading of why it is correct under the law, flagged: on the GameBoard the interval is a function of the state, the flight table, the collision table and the tables of the measured events are fixed, there is no draw, no register and no remainder at a Node (the draw left the board on 2026-09-18), and the interval is a bijection up to the click, so the same GameBoard always gives the same next GameBoard, and the past can be recovered. A detector is a set of Nodes with one record: the record is a sum over the set and over the arrivals, so it does not hold which Node clicked or which ray, and many GameBoards give the same record; the detector's world is what the records say, and from the records alone the next record is not determined, because what determines it is on the GameBoard and not in the record. That is the uncertainty in the detector's world: not a draw of nature, but the information a set's record does not carry; the uncertainty principle of A10 (a width times a momentum spread bounded below) is its measured form, and the phase a set takes after a click, the pointer's, is what the detector's world calls the quantum state's draw. The earlier statements of this document that "only a detector generates a draw" are read the same way: the draw is in the detector's world, the GameBoard has none.

### 16. The re-emitted ray keeps its family: "by the board's principle of preserving information this comes out by itself, no?"

A ray's record is what the ray is (Node, direction, age, phase, number, amount, content; the family is its identity and its rho is a key of the family), and a measured event's table can only read, measure, re-release or pass it: the mirror turns the ray, it does not rewrite it. There is no column for a factor, the books balance per family (a family change at the mirror would destroy content in one family's line and create it in another's), and the tables come from the keys, so a re-emitted ray pushes by its own family's rho and carries nothing of the mirror; no rule had to be added. The one field that changes at a re-emission is the number, which becomes the mirror's, so that the mirror does not read its own re-emissions under the one reading set; that change happens at a click, the one-way border, where the law allows it.

### 17. Why a proton and a neutron bind on the GameBoard today

**Why a proton and a neutron bind on the GameBoard today (the owner's question, 2026-09-20; the orchestrator's answer, flagged).** The one coupling is M_A (rho_A rho_B - 1) x flow; the neutron's rho is 0, so between a proton and a neutron only the -1 remains, a pure attraction in proportion to the reader's content and the other's flow (M / r^2), the same term that is gravity between every pair of families. It holds them only because the declared scale of the charge is small (with rho_p = 1 the electric push between two protons exactly cancels this term); at nature's scale (about 10^18 per unit of content in label units) the term is negligible and the pair would not bind without the sigma column, which is why the strong force is in design. The mechanics of the binding at one Link: each interval the two push toward each other, a step onto a Node that holds a measured event is refused, nothing is lost and nothing pushes back, so they stay at one Link. Found in the same reading, a defect for the strong-force design: at the refused step the momentum label stays and keeps growing inward every interval, without bound until the integer bound refuses the run, because the third law acts only through the rays and not at the contact; a contact rule is needed (the refused step handing its momentum component to the occupant, or the occupant reading the arriving body as a click of its table, or a repulsive core in sigma at zero distance), sent to the physicist's design of the strong force, together with the electron of width 3 reaching the proton.

### 18. Alpha on the GameBoard

**Alpha on the GameBoard (the owner, 2026-09-20: "these are good statements that explain alpha; explain alpha again"; the orchestrator's reading, flagged, sent to the strong-force design as expectations).** The alpha particle, two protons and two neutrons: between a proton and a neutron and between two neutrons only sigma pulls (at one Link, within the range L); between the two protons sigma pulls and the electric rho_p^2 pushes, net attraction at one Link only if sigma^2 > rho_p^2 - 1 and repulsion alone beyond L. On the cubic GameBoard the best cluster of four is the 2 x 2 square p n / n p: every proton touches two neutrons (four sigma bonds) and the two protons sit on the diagonal at sqrt 2, where the electric push is half its one-Link value and sigma reaches only if L >= 2; a corner or a line gives three bonds. Saturation comes from the range: a fifth nucleon on the square's side finds one or two bonds against the electric push of two protons, so He-5 and Li-5 should be unbound in the model as in nature. Alpha decay: in a nucleus of Z protons a surface alpha cluster is held by sigma through its L-neighbours only while the electric push of the other Z - 2 protons reaches it at 1 / r^2; when the push exceeds the hold the cluster is pushed out as one, since inside it sigma dominates; the GameBoard is deterministic and has no tunnelling, so a nucleus either holds or decays, and the only source of a spread of decay times in this law is the fan's grain, to be measured in series I. The mass defect is absent: a free ray carries no content and the alpha's content reads exactly 2 x 1836 + 2 x 1839. If "alpha" meant the fine-structure constant: it is the declared strength of the electric column, rho, and the law does not derive it.

### 19. "Information to the detector about a Node is a ray the detector sends, which returns to it, and then it measures again?"

**"Information to the detector about a Node is a ray the detector sends, which returns to it, and then it measures again?" (the owner, 2026-09-20).** Confirmed under the law and recorded. A detector is a set of Nodes with one record and reads only what arrives at its Nodes; there is no other channel, since the one reading set of every measured event is "everything at the Node but the reader's own number". So a detector learns of a distant Node in two ways only: from the rays the thing there releases by itself (its field or its radiation), or from a ray sent toward it (by the detector's own lamp or a lamp beside it) that the thing there re-releases or passes, read when it comes back or comes through. The returning ray is a new click at the set: a different ray (the re-release keeps its family, takes the mirror's number and starts its age at 0), read as amount, direction, age and phase, and the set takes the pointer's phase after the click. What the detector knows of the Node is exactly that: the direction its heading, the distance its age (the flight time, the age reading), the thing's phase and content in what came back; not which Node of the set clicked. And the sending is never free or passive: a paid unit costs the sender quantum x s (E = h f), and when the thing at the Node measures it, the unit's momentum pushes it, so looking at a thing moves it by the label of the ray used; the uncertainty of the detector's world (A10) is the measured form of this. The owner, going on: "So is information about a Node the detector sees still needed?" No: a detector declares only its own Nodes, its threshold, its reading and its window, and needs nothing of any other Node; "seeing" a Node is the arrival of rays from it. The host's diagnostics that read the dense arrays of the GameBoard (the shell readings of the tools) are not a detector and prove nothing physical. The owner, going on: "So why does it need information about the ray it sent?" It does not, and the law keeps none: a measured event's record is its own age, phase, momentum, content and owed count, with no memory of what it released; everything the detector learns is on the returning ray, whose age is the flight time since the re-release (a re-emission starts the age at 0, so the age is the one-way distance from the mirror), whose phase is the mirror's, and whose number is the mirror's, which is why the sender reads it at all under the one reading set (it never reads a ray of its own number). What the sending left on the sender is only its cost, quantum x s of content, in its own books.

### 32. Series G landed: the Hubble diagram behind the detector

**Series G landed: the Hubble diagram behind the detector (2026-09-20, the run).** Twenty-four sources thrown from the centre of a 301^3 cube at 0.05 c to 0.6 c, a family each, chains of four on the six axes, releasing toward the centre with their clock's phase; a detector of one Node at the centre reading `wave` with `reads: "age"`; six masses at one Link as the mass inside; two crowds (coasting and pushing) and the two clocks (scalar and age); the expectation written first. The detector reads the linear Hubble law by itself: z = v / c to 0.003 for every source of the coasting throw and H t_0 = 1.03, the Hubble time the age of the throw; the reading's formula 1 + z = (1 + k)(1 + v / c) within 2 % in 288 of 288, the Doppler of the throw times the emitter's clock and nothing else. At large distance the detector's curve falls below the coasting form of its own near fit in every run, so of the three forms the one observed today, q = -0.55, is the nearest in ten of twelve windows, against the expectation that it be outside everywhere: the detector sees the signature of an accelerating recession while nothing accelerates on the GameBoard (the coasting momenta within 3 %, the pushing ones falling 4 to 32 %). The resemblance comes from what the detector cannot see: in the coasting throw the sources' initial distances (each reads the Milne form shifted by its start, the far ones started three times farther out), in the pushing crowd the emitters' clocks (the inner sources sit in the thickest crowd and their clocks run slowest, k up to 0.07, reddening the near part and inflating the near fit's H; with the clock removed the Doppler part reads the deceleration, H t_0 < 1 in every window). With H fitted per form the three forms agree within 0.005 in z: at this precision the shape does not tell q = +0.5 from 0 from -0.55. The age clock bends nothing beyond the grain. 22 pinned readings inside, 26 outside, none moved. What the law lacked, registered: a straight throw off the axes (the step rule loses a coinciding step), a three-dimensional gravity of a crowd of points (a beam never dilutes, a fan misses the Nodes off its lines), a source that releases along its own motion without taking its row home, emitters' clocks that count only their own crowd, and a step rule whose whole part does not cluster under a changing momentum. ### 80. THE CLICK DEFINED BY WHAT IT DOES

### 82. ONE QUANTUM, FROM THE BIRTH TO THE CLICK

**ONE QUANTUM, FROM THE BIRTH TO THE CLICK (the owner, 2026-09-20; the standing form of principle 4, in ten points).** The owner's words: (1) Birth: the lamp releases one record with u, a number between 0 and 1, from its clock; u is written on the row; nobody sees it. (2) Split: at the splitter the row becomes two, with a Link between them, in contact; the quantum is now on two paths; still one quantum: the norm of the two rows together is one. (3) Journey: the rows move apart, the Link stretches; every step local. (4) Merge: if the two rows meet at the same Node in the same direction they sum: that is the interference; in a dark fringe the sum is zero, the row disappears there, the norm passes to the bright fringe. (5) Computation: on the detector every Node has |Sigma|^2; the GameBoard computed "how much quantum arrived here", cancellations included; every possibility is laid out. (6) Click: the detector arranges its Nodes on a ladder from 0 to 1 by |Sigma|^2 and asks where u is; there the whole quantum is absorbed; the message passes over the Link and the second row is deleted; one click, one energy, zero loss. (7) Why it looks random: u vanishes with the absorption, only "D1" remains; over births u is uniform and the clicks are distributed as |Sigma|^2; Born is ignorance of u. (8) What fixes what: the structure fixes the boundaries on the ladder, u fixes the segment; the same u and the same structure, the same click, always (tested); another structure, the boundaries move, the same u falls elsewhere (tested). (9) The wave is not on the GameBoard; it is the form a thousand clicks draw, because the click read a sum. (10) The non-local: the deletion of the second row at the click; it is far only because it moved away after it was tied; the tie was made in contact, at the split. In one sentence: one quantum is a record spread over all its paths, tied to itself, and gathered at the click at the place u and the structure fixed together. ### 89. WHAT THE PROTOTYPE MEASURED, AND WHAT THE INTEGER FINDING MEANS

**WHAT THE PROTOTYPE MEASURED, AND WHAT THE INTEGER FINDING MEANS (recorded at the owner's request, 2026-09-20; the current statement on S).** The prototype of issue #365 (comment 2; `scratchpad/amp/proto.py`, floats, one Link per interval, not the engine, no integer tables) measured: a 5 x 5 Mach-Zehnder with one quantum per birth over 64 birth phases and no draw, equal arms D1 64 / D2 0, a half turn on arm 2 0 / 64, a quarter turn 32 / 32, arm 2 longer by two Links 32 / 32, exactly one click per birth even when the parts arrive at different times; and a pair as one record (HH + VV) / sqrt 2 with one u, E = 1.000, 0.707, 0.000, -0.707 against cos 2(a - b), S = 2.8281 (2 sqrt 2 = 2.8284), marginals 0 on both sides at every setting, the same S with Bob first, Alice's marginal unmoved by Bob's setting. Not checked by it: the integers, the speed 1 / sqrt 3, the discrete phase at N = 64, the coupling to the engine. The design's integer check (docs/designs/amplitude-v1) gives the same Mach-Zehnder exactly and, for the pair at N = 64, S = 176/64 = 2.750, at N = 256 2.8125, at N = 1024 2.82812, the marginals 32/64 in all 4096 setting pairs; the 2.875 quoted earlier was the strict-crossing rounding of the u-cells, which also broke the marginals (33/64): an artefact, not a prediction. What the finding means: (1) the mechanism (the record's sum at the click, u choosing on the ladder) reproduces the quantum correlation exactly in the continuum, so the mechanism is right and the deficit is the phase circle's grain alone; (2) Born and no-signalling are structural, exact at every N with the nearest rungs, while the correlation is discretised; (3) the model predicts S below 2 sqrt 2 by at most 4/N, so the best measured S = 2.8276 +- 0.0008 bounds nature's N at roughly 4000 or more, excludes N = 64 as nature's N, and leaves the model standing with a larger N, which is the paper's claim in one number; (4) the engine's Bell acceptance test at N = 64 expects 176/64, not 2.83, and the runs at N = 1024 and 4096 show the convergence.

### 92. "NATURE COMMUNICATES WITH ITSELF BY CLICKS"

**"NATURE COMMUNICATES WITH ITSELF BY CLICKS" (the owner, 2026-09-20; recorded as the sentence on communication).** On the GameBoard nothing communicates: packets move to neighbours and carry no message, a splitter spreads them, a mass turns them, and every one of these can be undone and settles nothing. A fact exists only where a click removes possibilities and writes a row of the world; so what one part of nature knows of another is exactly the list of clicks between them, and everything else is possibility in transit. A body reads the crowd (the push, the meeting) reversibly, which is not a message but a shared computation; the message is the click. Where clicks are dense the parts of the world talk at every tick and the GameBoard is classical; where there are none nothing has been said and it is quantum (principle 8). Births are the questions, clicks the answers, the world the transcript.

### 93. HOW MANY BITS A CLICK CARRIES

**HOW MANY BITS A CLICK CARRIES (the owner's question, 2026-09-20; the orchestrator's derivation from the ladder, to be verified by the design's mathematician before it is claimed).** One click writes one row of the world: which cell of the record's ladder u fell in. The ladder has at most N cells, since u takes N values and a cell needs at least Total / 2N of the weight, so one record, one quantum, yields at most log2 N bits at its click: 6 at N = 64, 12 at N = 4096, and no more however many Nodes the detector has. The deletion at a distance carries 0 bits (the marginals exactly 1/2, no-signalling). A message between two parts of nature is therefore births chosen by the sender and clicks read by the receiver, at most log2 N bits per click, at one Link per interval. If the bound holds it is a prediction that meets experiment from the other side: a photon shown to carry b bits bounds nature's N at 2^b or more, alongside the Bell bound N >= about 4000 (12 bits); a photon carrying more than log2 N bits would falsify the model at that N.

### 97. K UNDER THE RECORD CLICK: the offers are the crowd, the click reads the shared phase

### 102. THE PAPER SESSION'S CHECKS (issue #368): S(N) is not monotone and not bounded by 4/N; records 89 and 93 superseded on those points; the tie, the tables' norm, the rotation, the windowed which-path, the phase bound

**THE PAPER SESSION'S CHECKS, issue #368 (2026-09-20; paper/click_model/checks/s_of_n.py and its output on the branch claude/paper-click-model; a computation from the design's formulas with the repository's own tables, not an engine run).** (1) S(N) at the CHSH labels for every N with 8 | N up to 4096: the design's bell.txt reproduced exactly (176/64, 720/256, 2896/1024), then: 252 of the 512 values of N give S above 2 sqrt 2 (N = 16 and 32 give 3, N = 128 gives 23/8, N = 96, 192, 384, 768 give 17/6); the powers of two from 512 through 4096 give exactly 181/64 = 2.828125; between them S(N) scatters on both sides (2.82443 to 2.83212 for N >= 1024). (1) The step rule reads floor(age x |p| / D) at the CURRENT momentum (BEAM_LAW note 17, "no remainder is kept"): under a falling momentum the count stands still for tens of intervals (a stall of 85) and then increments at every interval (a burst of 12 Links on consecutive intervals; s_px1 stepped at ticks 321, 322, 323, 325, 326 at a momentum of 0.019 Links per interval): faster than the ray, against "one speed", and the Links made equal age x v_now, a deceleration erasing distance made. WHY: LOCAL bounds the work per Node per interval (six neighbours, a fixed number of accumulators for a fixed K), so the total is linear in the active Nodes and, in the event-driven form (record 190), in the events; a rule reading beyond its neighbours would cost the board's size per Node, quadratic in all; VECTOR makes every step a fixed number of bounded-integer operations (a translation one add and one compare, a bilinear form k multiplications with a declared matrix, the division one operation), with no iteration inside a step, no root, no solver, no transcendental function, and gives the rows a closed form, so a row costs one operation per event and not one per interval, and the same operation runs on every row at once (the host's vectorisation); GENERIC makes one primitive serve every family, one code path and one table, so the cost per event is constant across kinds and the large world costs per event exactly what the small one costs, and one primitive is verified instead of one per family. THE LIMITS, stated: the count of events is what it is (a dense world has an event per interval per row); the click with several arms would cost N^k on the tensor form and is evaluated through its rank-2 factorisation (record 192); the host's own costs (the state's writing, the record's format, record 203) are outside the law and are cut separately. WHY A GENERIC SYSTEM RULED BY SMALL CONDITIONS FOLLOWS: under the three tests the only free numbers are the small declared integers of the family table and the width (a rate, a charge, a lifetime, a content; record 189) and the initial state; a large system has no parameter of its own and no rule of its own scale (Highlights 3.21 emergence, 3.22 scale independence), so every large-scale law is the iterate of the small local rule and every known formula is its limit (DERIVATIONS_BEAM.md); hence a small condition rules the whole: a change of one declared integer or one small rule (form A against form B, the aberration of a moving body's fan) propagates through the one primitive to every scale and moves the registered integers everywhere (47 worlds under form B), exactly and not as noise, because the integers carry and never average; this is the system's falsifiability: a wrong small condition is caught by the large system's pins, and a right one needs no large-scale insertion

THE ONE QUANTUM: yes, the click is the whole record, once: exclusivity is the ladder's, the record's entire amount to one cell whatever its size (the law of the bit, the thing or its shadow), so a record is the quantum and the click its one measurement; the quantum's size is the record's amount and, for a paid family, its cost h per unit (E = h f, the cost per phase step); a detector's threshold T sets how much cumulative weight a rung needs, the sensitivity, not the quantum's size; the equation in one line: click = Threshold_u( Rungs_T( Gram_G( Reading_R( record ) ) ) ), followed by one translation of the state

### 262. The owner's finding on the derivation of c, section 13.2 (a): an explicit error and a jump in the conclusion (the owner, 2026-09-21, about 04:45Z, in the paper session, relayed by the paper coordinator, translated: "there is an explicit error and also a jump in the conclusion in the derivation of the speed of light. In fact, to get from (0, 0, 0) to (1, 1, 1) three steps are needed and the displacement is sqrt 3, so the speed is sqrt 3 / 3 = 1 / sqrt 3. The jump: from this it follows that if one demands the same speed in every direction it must satisfy c <= 1 / sqrt 3; to get equality one must add that the speed realises the maximum possible. The owner's question on the method, "how do you derive these formulas?", and the physicist's answer: the infinite limit derives the form, the run confirms the number, the pin orders that the first be written before the second (2026-09-21, about 08:05Z; relayed by the physicist on the owner's "pass it to the Boss"; recorded at 08:15Z). The owner, translated: "explain to me in simple words how you derive these formulas; do you do it by the pin method to something? do you use the simulator and our formulas? how does it work?", and then: "aren't you trying the infinite limit to get a formula? because it is the infinite limit that gives the formula, so you can get their formulas from it, not only by the pin method." The physicist's answer, as given: yes; the limit is the derivation and the pin is only the discipline around it. (1) The integer rules are the given (the six verbs); every formula in DERIVATIONS_BEAM.md is the continuum limit of one rule, the grain fine, many rows, large distances, N, Q and P large: c = 1 / sqrt 3 is the limit of the accumulator against the wall, 1 / r^2 the limit of the shell's Node count, Born's rule the limit of the click's Gram form, Young's spacing the limit of the fan by angle, the Shapiro logarithm in optical-v1 the integral of M / r along the path; the known formula is what remains when the grain vanishes, and the finite-grain departures (the shell's ripple, u_d within 1.35 percent, the rungs) are the law's signature, not noise. (2) The pin does two things the limit cannot: it checks by one run that the finite law realises its limit at the registered widths (a formula gives, a run proves; record 205), and it keeps the work honest by writing nature's number and what the limit must give BEFORE the computation, so no constant is tuned backward; the comparison is always through a detector's reading. (3) The limit matters most where it gives a DIFFERENT formula from nature's: the owed count's limit is 1 / (1 + k) and not sqrt(1 - 2 k), the far lamp's brightness reads q_eff = +1, a moving clock reads 1 and not gamma; the limit cannot invent a term the rules do not have, so it shows exactly what is missing, which is what let the day say "the root is the seventh verb" and design optical-v1 with its one missing integer, the factor 2. (4) What it is not: Einstein's formulas are never put into the simulator, no parameter is fitted to data, a limit that differs from nature is registered as a FAIL in the same font as a PASS. Passed to the paper coordinator for the method section beside record 300's six-point standard (the limit taken and the order of the expansion are its points 2 and 3); nothing else changes.

### 366. The precedents study of the great papers delivered (the owner's order of record 356): the pattern the greats share in eight lines, our paper against it, and the verdict keep, change, adopt; published beside the paper (2026-09-21, 12:11Z; recorded by the Boss at 12:15Z). The research agent read fourteen papers (Newton's Principia Book III, Maxwell 1865, Boltzmann 1877, Planck 1900, Lorentz 1904, Einstein 1905 both papers, Bohr 1913, Einstein 1916, de Broglie 1924, Heisenberg 1925, Schrodinger 1926, Dirac 1928, Feynman 1948), primary texts where the session's proxy allowed (GitHub-hosted transcriptions; fourmilab, wikisource, archive.org, arxiv and every university host blocked), every quotation verbatim and cited, SECONDARY marked where only search snippets were readable (Lorentz, de Broglie, Heisenberg, Feynman); paper/general_formula/PRECEDENTS.md on the branch precedents-study (f7a44613), its PR opened by the Boss, docs only, the paper itself untouched. The pattern: the inputs first and few (two postulates, two assumptions, Rules and Phenomena, three kinds of facts); the new law in the author's voice and hedged ("I propose", "the theory here advanced", "as I believe"); the old laws named with their author and a plain verb ("first approximation", "equivalent to Newton's law", "accounts for the law connecting the lines", "the well-known Bohr energy levels arise", "just that assumed in the spinning electron model"); borrowed steps with a name and page or "as is well known"; experiment as whose measurement and which number ("inside the uncertainty", "agrees sufficiently well"); the miss admitted in the same paper with its cause (Bohr's Pickering lines, Einstein's red shift "still missing", Dirac's second difficulty); no great claims a known formula, the novelty claimed is the mechanism; own earlier work cited by section. Our paper against it: the ledger, the standing column, the four labels, the one prediction and the not-claimed list are the greats' items made explicit; the credits are by eponym or by name, year and bibitem; one factual mis-attribution: fig:square's "Einstein, 1905: E^2 = E_0^2 + p^2 c^2" is in neither 1905 paper (1905a gives W = m c^2 (1 / sqrt(1 - v^2 / c^2) - 1) and the two masses, 1905b L / c^2); the "contains and extends" words of the greats collected for the six places that stand above; the ledger, the FAIL table, the prediction table and the SHA record have precedents in kind but not in length. VERDICT: (1) KEEP the ledger of inputs, the standing column and four labels, the one prediction and the not-claimed list; (2) CHANGE fig:square to "the energy-momentum relation of special relativity" (no year) and its caption to the greats' verb ("gives ... exactly; the relation is not new"; the identity's own content the integer form, the departure the rounding of E', one part in E'_0, a row a measurement can refute); (3) CHANGE the abstract's "four pass, twelve fail" to carry the cause of the twelve in one clause (the law, a declared input, a hypothesis); (4) ADOPT one closing sentence in the greats' form at the end of the sections that reach a known formula (the author of the known law, the verb, one measured number with the experimenter's name, the gap admitted), one hedged sentence of newness in the Introduction, "as is well known" for a borrowed step; (5) ADOPT moving commit SHAs out of captions and Part II's text into Reproducibility and the appendix, and one-line bibitems for Shannon, Landauer, Bresenham and Jefimenko or the eponyms dropped. Sent to the coordinator for the wave after wave 14 with a referee round; the owner told the five lines.

Pages 24-27, references: the literature of the derivations, the methods and the experimental data. The paper coordinator (session_01299yiyFeoMygyRnALeMZer) relays the owner (translated in full): "Use only the things that are closed with us, that have a clear claim and a clear proof; throw out what is not clear; you know from the reviews what is clear and proved, use that. In my view the central thing in the paper is the claim that several different physical phenomena can be produced from one shared discrete update law and a small number of assumptions. The general formula is the starting point. The possible novelty lies in showing how the same mechanism leads to the geometry of propagation, to the flux and the forces, and further to measurement and to correlations. The decisive question is how many of the results the law really forces. If for every phenomenon a rule must be added that puts the desired result in beforehand, the law's explanatory power shrinks; if the same rules force several different results with little freedom of choice, that is the strong scientific contribution. So the three things must work together: the general formula defines the mechanism; the derivations show what follows from it and under what conditions; the simulator and the comparison with experiment check the results and their limits. In the version I read, the contribution that can be established now is an explicit model with several conditional mathematical results and numerical checks; the broad claim that it describes nature still needs completions. I would build the paper around a precise statement of the distance between these two."
